title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a 'Remarque' interrupting the construction of the déploiement (unfolding) of an equisingular stratification. The previous pages build spaces Σ_i and Σ_ij; the next page (§19) sketches heuristically how Σ_i and Σ_ij are built from tubular neighbourhoods.

The abstract structure. Grothendieck isolates a common structure: an 'ordered topological space' Σ, i.e. a poset object in Top. Write Σ(0)=Σ and Σ(1) for the space of strictly comparable pairs (graph of <). There are two projections, s and b, from Σ(1) to Σ(0). Three conditions are imposed:
- (a) s is a proper fibration.
- (b) b is a proper immersion.
- (c) the order is trivial on each connected component: x<y forces x and y into different components.
A marginal note says (c) follows from (a) and (b) under extra hypotheses on b and on the components (finite dimensionality, as on p.31). By (c), the strict order descends to Ĩ = π0(Σ). The previous page then describes the déploiement as such a Σ together with a strictly increasing map Ĩ → I.

The two contexts. The marginal note says 'déploiement' is used here in two rather different senses.
1. Naive unfolding. Σ = ⊔ X_i (closed strata) and Σ(1) = ⊔_{X_i⊂X_j} X_i. Here s is the identity of X_i into the i-th summand, hence étale and a finite covering (indeed more special). b is the closed inclusion X_i → X_j, which is very special.
2. Equisingular unfolding (the subject of the manuscript). Σ_i is the stratum X_i with an open tube around the smaller strata removed. Σ_ij is the boundary of a tube of Σ_i inside X_j, with the deeper strata cut out (p.32). Here s: Σ_ij → Σ_i is the linking-bundle projection, a proper fibration. b: Σ_ij → Σ_j is the inclusion of a boundary face ('bordant'), and s is much more special than a general fibration.

In both contexts the index poset I can be replaced by Ĩ = π0(Σ). In the first case this amounts to stratifying by connected components of the closed strata X_i. In the second it amounts to using components of the open strata X_i* = X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j.

Purpose. The page gives an intrinsic, index-free axiomatics of the unfolded object (a compact 'manifold with corners'-type system glued along fibrations and boundary immersions). It also shows that the indexing poset can always be canonically refined to π0.
errors: Condition (c) is stated as an axiom. Grothendieck's own margin claims it is a consequence of (a) and (b) only under extra unstated hypotheses; the derivation is not given and is not automatic in general.
The direction of s and b is left implicit. Comparison with the examples shows s goes to the smaller element and b to the larger; nothing is wrong, but it is never stated.

ideas.what: Encoding an unfolded stratified space as a poset internal to Top. Source map s is a proper fibration (linking-sphere bundle); target map b is a proper boundary immersion.
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping / resolution of a stratified space into a system of manifolds with corners; Thom–Mather abstract stratified space via its 'link bundle' data; topological poset / topological category model
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data, 1970); Verona; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzip' for conically smooth stratified spaces (2017); Lurie and Treumann for exit-path categories
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces 'déploiement' of stratified spaces and tubular neighbourhoods in tame topology, but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Two notions of déploiement: the naive one (disjoint union of closed strata with inclusion maps) and the equisingular one (strata with tubes removed, glued along link bundles). Both fit the same axioms, with the roles of s and b being 'special' exchanged.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of the closed-strata (Čech-type) diagram with the link-bundle / exit-path model of a stratified space

ideas.what: Replacing the index poset I by Ĩ = π0(Σ): components of closed strata, or components of open strata, with a strictly increasing map Ĩ → I.
ideas.modern_name: Refinement of a poset-stratification to its connected-component stratification

missed.claim: Grothendieck axiomatizes the unfolded stratified space as an ordered topological space: s is a proper fibration onto the smaller stratum piece, b a proper (boundary) immersion into the larger, and the order is trivial on components. He observes that the naive closed-strata diagram satisfies the same axioms with the roles of 'special' exchanged (s étale, b closed immersion). This prefigures the AFT 'unzipping' picture and exit-path/topological-poset models. The explicit duality between the two models as instances of one structure is not, to my knowledge, formulated in the literature.
missed.quote: Dans deux contextes différents ... on a rencontré des espaces topologiques ordonnés Σ, satisfaisant les conditions suivantes a) ... fibration propre b) ... immersion propre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a single category of 'unfolding data' (poset objects in Top with fibration and immersion legs) containing both the Čech-type closed-strata diagram and the conical/link-bundle resolution. This could help compare models of stratified homotopy types (Douteau, Haine, Nand-Lal, AFT).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean conceptual axiomatization of the déploiement as an internal poset in Top, in an unpublished manuscript, anticipating later unzipping and exit-path frameworks. However, it is a short remark, the ideas largely reappear independently in Thom–Mather and AFT, and the déploiement program itself was announced in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Margin: '* en deux sens assez différents' is a footnote to 'déploiement'. The struck word before 'stratification' is unreadable.
Line a) reads 'Σ(1) →s Σ(0) = Σ(0)'; the subscript '(1)' vs '(1)' notation varies.
c) should read 'Si x,y ∈ Σ sont dans une même composante connexe, alors x ≤ y ⇒ x = y (i.e. si x,y ∈ Σ, x<y, alors x,y sont dans des composantes connexes différentes)'.
Margin near c): 'conséquence de a) b) si on suppose que Σ(1) →b Σ(0) est ... et que les composantes de Σ sont de dim. finie...'.
'l'exemple certain' is probably 'l'exemple trivial/naïf'; the word is uncertain.
's est étale, revêtement fini dans ...)' rather than 'couvrant fini'.
'bien plus spécial pour b' and 'bien plus spécial pour s', rather than 'bien des spécial'.
'on peut expliquer la variété des Î' is likely 'on peut remplacer I par Ĩ = π0(Σ)'. The symbol is Ĩ (tilde), not Î.
